title: Implementing a custom ParamType: required members, failure and completion hooks
answers: What must a custom ParamType implement?
How do ParamType failures get reported?
How do metavar and shell completion work for a ParamType?
body:
- `types.py:ParamType` is a generic ABC (`ParamType[T]`, 8.4.0). Subclass must set class attr `name` and implement `convert(value, param, ctx)`.
- `convert` must accept already-converted values and must work when `param` and `ctx` are None (prompt input).
- Failure: call `self.fail(message, param, ctx)` in `types.py:ParamType.fail`, which raises `BadParameter`.
- Optional overrides: `get_metavar(param, ctx)` (returns str|None), `get_missing_message(param, ctx)` (used by `exceptions.py` when a required value is missing, at ~line 201 via `self.param.type.get_missing_message`; Choice overrides it), `shell_complete(ctx, param, incomplete)`, `split_envvar_value`, `to_info_dict`.
- Composite types: subclass `CompositeParamType` (`is_composite=True`, `arity` property) so `type_cast_value` passes the whole value.
- Parameter-level completion: `core.py:Parameter.shell_complete` calls the custom `shell_complete` callback if given, else `self.type.shell_complete(ctx, self, incomplete)`.
